Blackjack it is — the classic house game. Quick recap: two cards each, dealer shows one card with the other face down. Cards are worth their pip value, faces count 10, and an Ace is 1 or 11. A natural (Ace + ten-card) on the deal ends the round instantly for 3:2, unless the dealer also has one (a push). Otherwise you act first — hit, stand, double, or split a pair — then the dealer reveals and draws to 17, standing on all 17s. Blackjack pays 3:2, a plain win pays even money, ties push.

You're starting with a 1,000 chip bankroll. Set your bet to open the first round.

blackjack, 21, hit, stand, double, split — the classic house game

Two cards each; dealer shows one, hole card face-down. Values: pips as printed, faces 10, Ace 1 or 11. A natural (Ace + ten-card on the deal) ends the round at once: reveal the hole card, settle it (3:2 unless the dealer also has 21, then a push), and offer no hit, stand or double. Otherwise the player acts first: hit, stand, double (one card, doubled stake), split pairs; over 21 busts immediately. Dealer then reveals and draws to 17, standing on all 17s. Blackjack (Ace + ten-card) pays 3:2, a win pays 1:1, equal totals push.
